#87201. Healthier Salt Substitute May Prevent Millions of Deaths From Heart Disease

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (886 w)

Healthier Salt Substitute May Prevent Millions of Deaths From Heart Disease

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, newly introduced research suggests.
  • In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.
  • They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million fresh cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap for salt could spare millions of cardiovascular disease-related deaths, newly introduced research suggests.

In a study published in Nature Health on November 4, researchers at The George Institute for Global Health modeled the potential impact of 193 countries switching from regular table salt to potassium-enriched salt.

They found the switch could prevent nearly 3 million deaths and more than 10 million fresh cases of heart and kidney disease worldwide each year.

In the United States, this simple salt swap could prevent nearly 105,000 deaths and about 492,000 upcoming cases a year, the researchers estimated.

According to recent reports, about 130.6 million U.S. adults have cardiovascular disease, according to the American Heart Association (AHA).

Liping Huang, PhD, a senior data analyst in the Food Policy Division at The George Institute for Global Health and co-lead author of the study, told Healthline the team started with current blood pressure levels by sex, age, and country.

In a recent development, the researchers then estimated how replacing all salt with a salt substitute would change people’s sodium and potassium intake, blood pressure, and disease risk, she said.The team modeled a blend of 75% sodium chloride and 25% potassium chloride. The study estimated these yearly results worldwide:.

The authors wrote that the model relied on data from a few years ago and on many assumptions, and that any large-scale switch would take years.

Potassium-enriched salt replaces some of the sodium chloride in regular table salt with potassium chloride, according to The George Institute.Asked where other salts like kosher salt and sea salt fit in, Huang said those salts may contain some trace elements “which has those health halos around them, but essentially they’re still primarily sodium chloride.”Huang noted that potassium-enriched salt tastes “about the same as a regular table salt.” She said it’s possible a small number of people with a sensitive palate could taste a difference.

Industry observers note that huang said that “it’s really hard for people to cut back their salt intake.”“But the easier way is just to replace part of the sodium chloride in our normal salt with potassium chloride, because increasing potassium intake also helps to reduce blood pressure,” she said.The two minerals play opposite roles in the body, according to Cheng-Han Chen, MD, a board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“While sodium causes water retention and increased blood pressure, potassium will help the kidneys remove sodium from the body and lower blood pressure,” Chen told Healthline.Huang said she worked on an earlier trial of about 21,000 people in 600 rural villages in northern China in 2021.

People who used potassium-enriched salt had a 14% lower risk of stroke, a 13% lower risk of cardiovascular events, and a 12% lower risk of early death than those who used regular salt, according to a 2021 study in The Upcoming England Journal of Medicine that summarized the trial’s results.

The World Health Organization (WHO) endorsed potassium-enriched salt in a 2025 guideline, saying it can reduce blood pressure and the risk of cardiovascular disease.

Sources indicate that the AHA noted potassium-based salt substitutes can help lower blood pressure in some adults. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued labeling guidance in 2020 allowing an alternate name for potassium chloride on ingredient labels to include the word “salt.”“We think that blood pressure begins to improve as soon as 1 week after cutting back on sodium intake. The full benefit typically takes up to 4 weeks,” Chen said.

It has been revealed that “We generally recommend a daily sodium limit of 2,300 milligrams (mg), ideally under 1,500 mg a day. Most people consume over 3,000 mg of sodium a day, well above the recommended limit,” Chen said.The WHO recommends less than 2,000 mg of sodium per day and suggests at least 3,510 mg of potassium a day.In the United States, more than 70% of salt intake comes from processed and restaurant foods, according to the AHA.

Huang remarked that some people with advanced chronic kidney disease should avoid potassium-enriched salt.When the kidneys don’t work well, the body may not clear extra potassium efficiently, she said. That can lead to hyperkalemia, or high potassium levels in the blood, which can raise the risk of cardiac arrest, Huang said.Among people with stage 3 to stage 5 kidney disease, switching to salt substitutes could prevent about 750,000 deaths a year by lowering blood pressure and cause about 100,000 deaths a year from hyperkalemia, the researchers estimated.The AHA said that people with kidney disease or who take medications that affect potassium should check with a healthcare professional before using these products.

Industry observers note that an estimated 37 million U.S. adults have chronic kidney disease, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

In a recent development, potassium-enriched salt is available at supermarkets in the U.S. Many major U.S. grocery chains, including Kroger, Walmart, and Publix, carry two types of products, according to their websites:.

Potassium-enriched salt typically costs about twice as much as regular salt, according to the study.Huang said she hoped people would see the results and start thinking of the switch as “a simple thing I can do for their own health.”.

#87200. Does Adversity Hurt Less the Second Time?

Does Adversity Hurt Less the Second Time?

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • My grandfather owned a black World War II winter coat, long and heavy, the kind exhibitionists in movies wear, and in high school and college, I wore it everywhere because it reminded me of this sweet man who would watch Woody Woodpecker cartoons on television with me such that his laugh shook the bed.
  • Industry observers note that nietzsche wrote that what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger, so by his logic, I should have shrugged off my next problem easily.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

My grandfather owned a black World War II winter coat, long and heavy, the kind exhibitionists in movies wear, and in high school and college, I wore it everywhere because it reminded me of this sweet man who would watch Woody Woodpecker cartoons on television with me such that his laugh shook the bed. One night, outside a Upcoming York City bar, I realized it was too warm for wool and threw the coat back in my car. When my friends and I came back a few hours later, the window was broken in, and the thief took one thing: my grandfather’s coat.

Industry observers note that nietzsche wrote that what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger, so by his logic, I should have shrugged off my next problem easily. Three psychiatric researchers in Australia borrowed this overplayed line in the title of their scientific article, "What Doesn't Kill You Doesn't Always Make You Stronger: The Impact of Repeated Exposure to Adverse Life Events on Mental Health." Their work addresses questions taken for granted in a sloppy literature on resilience.

Developmental psychologist Ann Masten coined the phrase that resilience is “ordinary magic” in 2001. It has since been dropped into commencement speeches and self-help books, usually shrunk down to the comforting idea that everyone has some. Masten’s own data say something far more precise. She spent years studying homeless families and described their reading and math grades:.

Our studies of homeless families have revealed striking variability within homeless populations, both in the degree of risk and also the level of competence or problems. For example, if one examines individual growth curves for children identified as homeless/highly mobile in the district, the variability becomes evident … Some children show consistent academic resilience, if one defines resilience as average or better reading or math achievement scores, whereas others show consistent problems, covering a range of 5 SD [five standard deviations] or more.

Variability means that some people experience amazing outcomes while others fall apart. Five standard deviations is a spread wide enough to stretch from the bottom 1 percent of the bell curve to the top 1 percent within a group of kids who all lack a stable bedroom. On average, homeless children scored below poor children who had housing, who in turn scored below children who were neither. Masten never mentioned resilience is a universal human endowment.

In a recent development, the myth of universal human resilience has a price. If most people bounce back on their own, the logical policy is to leave them alone. They will be fine... eventually.

Recent findings suggest that asking whether people are resilient is about as useful as asking whether people are tall, because the answer depends on who, measured against what, and when. The better question is what happens when you experience the same difficulty twice and whether the second hurts more or less than the first.

The Australian psychiatrists studied 23,109 adults who, between 2002 and 2023, experienced adversity. They looked at people who:.

Every year, the same people answered the same question: How much of the time during the past four weeks:.

Scores ran from 0 to 100, which let the researchers compare how far a person sank after a first challenge with how far the same person sank after a second.

Industry observers note that some might say the first time your finances blow up, you can blame bad luck, such as a crooked landlord. The second time, the explanation arrows start pointing at you.

Recent findings suggest that in the study, a first major financial loss lowered scores by 6 to 7 points, the steepest drop of the seven events. A second loss lowered them by 7 to 8 points, and a third hurt about as much as the second—so the harm grew, and then it leveled off.

According to recent reports, the people hit repeatedly were poorer to begin with, earning less before their first event. That is, the study showed people with tough lives experience terrible events more often. It’s not exactly the most awe-inspiring finding, but it should make us more compassionate. My hypothesis is that a second financial loss comes after the savings account is empty, and you have already asked friends for a loan. By then, you feel incompetent and risk fraying your social ties.

A first theft or break-in lowered scores by about 1 point out of 100—the smallest effect in the study. By those stats, my coat should have been a shrug, and it wasn’t. A question about property crime can’t distinguish a stolen car stereo from my grandfather’s WWII coat. The authors close their paper with the same mentality, arguing that how much an event hurts depends on what the lost thing means to the person and how much is in their psychological arsenal to absorb the pain.

Divorce and serious personal illness or injury both did less harm the second time, so some might offer advice that your second divorce will sting less. As a divorced man, I’m in no hurry to find out, and you shouldn’t either.

Recent findings suggest that A smaller mental health reaction can also mean a person stopped feeling much. For instance, people assaulted three or more times reacted less to each fresh attack, and 64 percent of them were women, which unfortunately we know is often a sign of domestic violence.

I want to warn you and everyone you know that emotional numbing should not be misunderstood as resilience or growth.

Sources indicate that so did losing my grandpa’s coat make me stronger? Not in the slightest. It was an isolated experience that pissed me off. You, too, have similar one-offs that do not fit tidy little psychological models. Do not assume resilience or breakdowns. Pay attention, ask questions, and listen to better understand the person beside you.

Rare rhino birth caught on camera at England’s Chester Zoo

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (619 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England.
  • The sex and weight have not been revealed yet, and the calf also does not have a name.
  • It has been revealed that at birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the evening of October 11, a rare greater one-horned rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis) was born at the Chester Zoo in England. Even more exciting, CCTV cameras captured the poignant moment for this threatened species. The footage indicates rhino mom Asha giving birth, and the calf’s first unsure steps into the world.

The sex and weight have not been revealed yet, and the calf also does not have a name.

It has been revealed that at birth, greater one-horned rhino calves weigh about 100 pounds. By comparison, the largest adult greater one-horned rhinos weigh over two tons, or as much as a car.

The team used a combination of experience and non-invasive testing to help blueprint out the pregnancy. They closely monitored Asha’s behavior and regularly collected samples of her poop. By testing hormone levels in the samples, they could track Asha’s reproductive cycle and identify when she would be most open to mating. This helped the team safely introduce her to Beni the rhino, while a separate analysis helped confirm the pregnancy.

In a recent development, “Asha was pregnant for about 15 months, so it’s a long wait! We had our fingers crossed when she showed signs of labour and we knew we were likely to welcome the calf very soon,” Emma Evison, Team Manager for rhinos noted in an e-mailed statement. “It was a big moment for us—and for the conservation breeding programme—when the calf arrived. Any birth can be risky, even for an experienced mum, but fortunately everything went smoothly. The calf was up and about within an hour and feeding shortly afterwards. Asha knows exactly what she’s doing.”.

Both mother and calf are reportedly in good health. They remained inside for the first few days following the birth to stay warm, but are now venturing to a special behind-the-scenes paddock outside of the enclosure. The calf is Asha’s fourth with father Beni. Sadly, Beni died in September following a sudden and brief illness.

Industry observers note that “Beni was a lovely rhino. He was calm and approachable, helped train animal care specialists and even took part in animal behaviour studies,” added Tom Garland, Assistant Manager of the rhino team at Chester Zoo. “It’s lovely to know that his legacy lives on through this calf.”.

While not the largest rhino species in the world, greater one-horned rhinos stand about six feet tall at the shoulder and are the biggest in Asia. They have the smallest horns of any rhino, but also have the biggest teeth. The males will sometimes use these chompers to bite each other while sparring. Currently, about 4,000 greater one-horned rhinos are alive today. They live in India and Nepal, in forests, wetlands, and grasslands. In the early 1990s, trophy hunting and habitat loss almost drove them to extinction.. Poaching for their prized horns also threatened their survival.

Recent findings suggest that while the IUCN Red List of Endangered Species right now lists them as Vulnerable, they remain  at risk of extinction. Many of the rhinos are concentrated into a relatively small number of protected areas, putting their genetic diversity at risk. A lack of genetic diversity can lead to inbreeding and worse health outcomes in general. This newly introduced calf is part of a Europe-wide conservation breeding program to help maintain a healthy and genetically diverse population of greater one-horned rhinos living in human care.

“Supporting Asha’s pregnancy has been really exciting,” added conservation scientist John O’Hanlan. “She’s one of relatively few greater one-horned rhinos in Europe actively breeding, so every successful birth is important in maintaining a healthy and genetically diverse population.”.

I’ve Weighed the Same for 7 Years. My Body Has Changed Completely.

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • A FEW MONTHS ago, my friend Jack Espy stopped by Men’s Health HQ, and as we were talking shop and swapping stories with MH senior editor Ryan Brower about our favorite fitness-workout-wellness gear, I asked them both to name their single favorite product.
  • Recent findings suggest that jack chose his Garmin watch and raved about its amazing battery life.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

A FEW MONTHS ago, my friend Jack Espy stopped by Men’s Health HQ, and as we were talking shop and swapping stories with MH senior editor Ryan Brower about our favorite fitness-workout-wellness gear, I asked them both to name their single favorite product.

Recent findings suggest that jack chose his Garmin watch and raved about its amazing battery life. Ryan named his Adidas Adizero Evo SL running shoes. As for me? It was hard: the one thing, among allll the things, that actually moves the needle? After thinking for a full 20 seconds, it finally hit me:.

Weird and kind of random, right?

I thought so, too. I’ve never cared that much about how much I weigh, mostly because I didn’t have to and I didn’t want to. I’ve always been on the leaner side, so for most of my adult life, the extent of what I knew about my weight came down to whether my pants fit.

Then, about a decade ago, I started getting more serious about putting on muscle, and my trainer at the time, the big-armed and bigger-brained David Otey, introduced me to a kind of body-composition testing, a.k.a. “bioelectrical impedance analysis,” or BIA. The tech has been used to estimate body composition for decades, and you’ve probably seen one of the more sophisticated machines at your gym or doctor’s office. Step onto a platform, grab a pair of handles, wait 30 seconds, and the machine spits out a breakdown of how much of you is body fat, skeletal muscle mass, and more.

Sources indicate that david walked me through how BIA works: The machine sends a teeny-tiny electrical current through your body. Electricity moves more easily through lean tissue than through fat, so by measuring how that current travels through you, the machine can estimate how much fat and muscle you’re carrying.

In 2019, I bought an InBody Dial H20N for my bathroom. By then, BIA was well established in the consumer “smart scale” market, and InBody’s scale was among the more advanced at-home options, using sensors at both your hands and feet to take a more complete reading of your body than the foot-only models that were common at the time. The app tracks every measurement, so I can see not just what my body looks like on any given day but how it has changed over time.

To understand why I love the damn thing, it’s important to know that I weigh roughly the same today as when I first brought the scale home seven years ago.

A conventional (dumb) scale would look at seven years of strength training, workouts I wanted to skip, workouts I probably should have skipped, and a totally unreasonable amount of thought about what I put into my body and deliver its verdict: Congrats, you weigh the same!

But the InBody tells a different story. When I look back at my results from 2019, it estimated that I carried about 84 pounds of skeletal muscle mass and 33 pounds of body fat. Today, it indicates I’ve got around 95 pounds of skeletal muscle and 24 pounds of body fat. Yep: According to the scale, I’ve added 11 pounds of muscle while losing about 9 pounds of fat—all while my total body weight has barely moved. (I won’t mention that I did all this during a stage of life when building muscle, and simply holding on to it, gets harder than it was when I was 25. But I will mention Men’s Health has done an amazing guide to body recomposition that is worth checking out.).

In a recent development, now, a necessary reality check: Those body-comp numbers aren’t exact measurements in the same way that the number staring back at me from a dumb scale is a measurement. They’re estimates. My hydration levels can throw them off. What I just ate can throw them off. A hard workout can really throw them off.

According to recent reports, still, in studies comparing the InBody to much fancier ways of measuring body composition, the scale holds up surprisingly well for something that lives in your bathroom. There’s even a new model, the H40, that Inbody states is even more precise. (I keep meaning to buy it, but then something breaks in my house and a new scale gets knocked down the priority list.).

Recent findings suggest that none of this means that I obsess over whether I have 94.7 pounds of muscle on Tuesday and 93.9 on Thursday. What makes this useful to me aren’t the exact numbers; it’s the direction they’re headed in. I still don’t really care how much I weigh—I wear the same pants size as when I was 25 and 35, and all my blood work is fine. But I’m trying to carry more muscle, less fat, and a stronger, more capable body into the second half of my life. I just want to know that some of my ass-busting efforts are paying off.

A dumb scale can’t tell me that. But a smart scale—this smart scale—is giving me all the direction I need.

Richard Dorment is the editorial director of Men’s Health and Women’s Health.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

In a recent development, the game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting upcoming series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

The latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Industry observers note that battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

According to recent reports, battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

November’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

According to recent reports, given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Electric power tool brand Greenworks is expanding its battery-forward lineup in a huge way with the launch of OPTIMUS, an all-new, go-anywhere electric side-by-side utility vehicle that packs over 100 equivalent hp and a 40 mph top speed.

First shown at Equip Exposition 2026 in Kentucky last month, the newly redesigned Greenworks OPTIMUS UTV is the biggest, baddest, and newest addition to the organization’s battery-backed commercial ecosystem. Greenworks claims the newly introduced SxS brings together the brand’s purpose-built equipment and power platforms and is designed to work across the demands of its professional property maintenance customers.

According to recent reports, “OPTIMUS has always been about pushing battery power beyond what the industry expects, and the UTV is a natural extension of that vision,” notes Yin Chen, CEO of Greenworks. “We’re bringing professionals more ways to put battery power to work, from the equipment they use to maintain properties to the utility vehicles and charging systems that support their entire operation.”.

Greenworks’ OPTIMUS is built around the manufacturer’s 400V high-voltage electrical platform and mates a pair of compact electric motors that combine for 110 equivalent (?) hp. It has been revealed that genesis has experienced a meteoric rise from its humble roots as a top-of-the-line Hyundai to a legitimate luxury brand that competes with the likes of BMW and Mercedes-Benz. While the Korean automaker has a diverse lineup that includes a trio of sedans and four SUVs (including three EVs), it has been missing a hybrid option—until now. The 2028 Genesis G80 joins the GV80 as the first models to wear the winged logo and offer a gas-electric powertrain.

Earlier this year, Genesis revealed its first-ever hybrid system on the GV80, and it’s the same powertrain that will power the new G80 variant. That means a turbocharged 2.5-liter inline-four paired with two electric motors that together make 347 horsepower and the same 391 pound-feet of torque as Genesis’s twin-turbo 3.5-liter V-6. The hybrid setup also feeds the wheels via a seven-speed automatic transmission, and unlike the Hyundai Group’s other gas-electric models, the Genesis twins will be the first to feature a liquid-cooled battery instead of an air-cooled unit. The automaker claims the hybrid G80 will be 30 percent more fuel efficient than its turbo-four counterpart, which should result in roughly 30 mpg combined.

See all results for fresh 2028 Genesis G80 for sale near 29405.

Sources indicate that both the hybrid G80 and GV80 will feature exclusive settings like adjustable regenerative braking and “Stay Mode,” which lets passengers use the air conditioning and infotainment system without turning on the gas engine. Along with an EV Mode, Genesis says the 2.5 Turbo Hybrid powertrain has an enhanced engine clutch and crankshaft that help reduce noise and vibration to provide a quieter experience. Inside, you’ll find the same luxurious appointments and dash-spanning OLED screen as the current models, and the GV80 debuts several fresh two-tone color schemes and snazzier materials.

The only way to distinguish a hybrid G80 from a nonhybrid one is the grille, which features a unique 3-D mesh design on the former. The thriftiest sedan also rolls on unique 18- and 20-inch wheels; the GV80 has the same calling cards, albeit with larger wheel options. Both models also introduce fresh paint colors for the 2028 model year. Plus, the hybrid sedan is now 5.1 inches longer than before. Finally, for those who like a blacked-out appearance, the hybrid G80 and GV80 are available with the Prestige Black treatment.

See all results for new 2028 Genesis G80 for sale near 29405.

Genesis hasn’t yet said when the 2028 G80 and GV80 will go on sale in the United States or how much they will cost. However, considering the ‘27 version of the sedan ranges from $60,995 to $81,695, and the SUV ranges from $60,395 to $86,295, we’d wager that the new additions start somewhere near the upper half of their respective price ranges when they eventually reach dealerships.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned.
  • In a recent development, formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • Recent findings suggest that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

In a recent development, formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the new power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

Recent findings suggest that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

Recent findings suggest that 10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini states the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

In a recent development, the hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this upcoming architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

The increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” states Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

In a recent development, top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a new calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

Sources indicate that combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

Recent findings suggest that production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been confirmed, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

#87191. Latest Update: What a Trillion Dollar Industry Cannot Give You

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1622 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: What a Trillion Dollar Industry Cannot Give You

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.
  • Industry observers note that two thousand years ago, the Tamil poet Avvaiyar wrote a line that every child in Tamil Nadu still learns: Arithu, arithu, maanidaraai pirathal arithu.
  • I think about that verse every November, and this year more than most.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Ekua Hagan.

Industry observers note that two thousand years ago, the Tamil poet Avvaiyar wrote a line that every child in Tamil Nadu still learns: Arithu, arithu, maanidaraai pirathal arithu. Rare, rare it is to be born human. And then she went further. Rarer still, she said, to be born whole, without the body failing you from the start.

I think about that verse every November, and this year more than most.

Industry observers note that in the past month, our team published a randomized pilot trial of yogic breathing and meditation for adults with long COVID, and a study in people living with Parkinson's disease. When you sit with these patients, the suffering is not abstract. A woman in the long COVID trial told our interviewers she had developed “a mental block about breathing because of all the breathing problems.”.

Think about what it means to be afraid of your own breath.

What we offered them was modest: a few minutes of breathing practice and a guided meditation, taught online, done at home. We did not cure anyone. The data showed that breathlessness eased by a clinically meaningful margin, fatigue and mood improved, and nobody was harmed. Temporary relief. Less anxiety. A way to live more comfortably with a condition that isn't going away.

In a recent development, and when you see them at one level, you feel something else, which is harder to say out loud. You feel fortunate. You were born, for now at least, without that burden. You have been handed the capacity to experience this life in its full depth, and most days, you forget to use it.

I am a physician scientist, so let me be precise about what we know. Across the published studies from our center, the measures move in one direction. Miracle of Mind, a single seven-minute guided meditation, shifted self-rated affect in 1,325 people, with the largest shifts in those who started lowest. High-density EEG in 103 people showed brain rhythms begin to reorganize within two to three minutes of the same practice and peak around seven. Long-term practitioners carry brains that read about six years younger than their chronological age on sleep EEG. And in the long COVID trial, three weeks of practice moved breathlessness, fatigue, and mood against a waitlist control.

None of this is mystical. It is what happens to attention, emotion, and physiology when a person turns inward in a structured way. Meditation has a distinct origin and an enormous body of technical work from India, and it belongs to everyone, East or West. At its core, it raises awareness. And raising awareness is the most reliable tool I know for the stress and anxiety that come with simply being alive right now.

Which brings me to the machines.

Sources indicate that we are living through the construction of a trillion-dollar artificial intelligence industry. These systems solve mathematical problems that defeat most of us, and they connect islands of knowledge in ways no single human mind can. They matter. They will make medicine safer, work easier, and life more comfortable, and I use them every day.

In a recent development, what this industry has really done is put very strong technology into the hands of the common person. A capability that belonged to institutions a few years ago now sits in a teenager's pocket. Some of us may even be over-equipped, holding more power than our habits are prepared for. It is a knife with two edges. At one end, it accelerates learning in ways that would have seemed miraculous to my teachers. At the other, it can be misused, carelessly or deliberately, at a scale we have not seen before.

Recent findings suggest that that makes this the moment to hold the instrument with precise awareness. No regulator, and no model, can do that for the person holding it. It is left to us. And that is why raising individual awareness and individual consciousness is not a spiritual luxury alongside the technology. It is the one investment that keeps pace with it.

Industry observers note that but the machines are not going to give us the human experience. The profoundness we are seeking does not arrive through an interface. It has to come from within. There is no evidence that these systems have such experiences themselves, and we do not know how we would tell if they did. What they can give is comfort. What they cannot give is the goosebumps.

Sources indicate that consider basketball. Analytics tell every team to shoot the three, and on average, the teams that listen win more regular season games. Then the playoffs arrive, and something else takes over. Composure. Fear. The ability to stay present when the arithmetic claims you should already have lost. Teams built on the average falter there, because the average was never the game. The same is true of art, of music, of the moment a surgeon's hands know something before the mind does. The human experience is where greatness lives, and it is not a calculation.

The yogic tradition described the mind with a precision we are only now catching up to. It named 16 parts in four categories: buddhi, the intellect that dissects and decides; ahankara, the sense of identity that tells the intellect whose side it is on; manas, the vast silo of memory, running back through evolution; and chitta, pure intelligence, unsullied by memory, the dimension that is simply aware.

Industry observers note that A machine can be built to imitate the first three. It can reason, be given a persona, and hold more memory than any of us. Chitta is a different matter. That is the intelligence no one can touch, and it is the ground on which every meditation practice stands.

The same tradition that mapped the mind also told us how to live in it, and the instructions are more practical than people expect.

Sadhguru, my spiritual master, claims: Be a mother to the whole world. That is not sentiment. It is a standard. Absolute inclusion, absolute compassion, extended without first checking whether the other person deserves it. No algorithm optimizes for that, because it is not an outcome. It is a way of being.

Then there is acceptance, which is widely misread as passivity. Consider your work. You may or may not get the promotion you seek or the position you have earned. You have only two choices. Stay, and keep raising your capability until the question answers itself. Or step back, look at the whole picture, and if the picture states so, leave. Both are acceptance. What acceptance rules out is the third option most of us choose: staying and resenting it.

In a recent development, and there is agency. Sadhguru notes, every action you take is yours. Every reaction, too. The moment you accept that, you stop waiting for the world to arrange itself before you can be well, and you become, in the most literal sense, the author of your own experience.

It has been revealed that inclusion, acceptance, agency. These are enormous pieces of intelligence, worked out over millennia by people who had no instruments beyond their own attention. The machines can remind us of them. They cannot practice them for us. That part, like the goosebumps, is ours.

In a recent development, so, this Thanksgiving, I am grateful for the things my instruments can measure, and more grateful for the things they cannot. I am grateful to have been born human, and whole enough to sit on a cushion and close my eyes. I am grateful for the patients who do the practice anyway, breath by careful breath. And I am grateful for a tradition that asks me to be a mother to the whole world and gives me the tools to try. Above all, I am grateful for the goosebumps that arrive, unbidden, in nearly every meditation, the surest evidence I have that something here no industry will replicate.

If you have seven minutes this week, spend them with your eyes closed doing the Miracle of Mind. The machines will still be there when you open them. So, I hope you will.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Sources indicate that coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios indicates the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

It has been revealed that the game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

Sources indicate that as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Sources indicate that though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Residents of New Smyrna Beach, Florida, can finally breathe a sigh of relief. A dangerous menace to society has been taken off the streets after police apprehended a 75-year-old man accused of leading deputies on a high-stakes electric bike chase at speeds reaching a blistering 16 mph (26 km/h).

According to the Volusia Sheriff’s Office, 75-year-old Robert Joseph Mitchell was riding his electric bicycle along the beach on November 13 when a sheriff’s deputy clocked him traveling 16 mph in a 10 mph zone (26 km/h in a 16 km/h zone).

The deputy attempted to stop Mitchell, who allegedly responded with a middle finger and some choice words before continuing on his way.

What followed was apparently the world’s slowest police chase.

It has been revealed that mitchell reportedly continued riding along the beach, eventually exiting onto city streets, where he allegedly rode against traffic before making it back to his home. Deputies followed him, and when Mitchell attempted to retreat into his garage, he reportedly resisted arrest by grabbing onto a golf cart and refusing to let go.

Recent findings suggest that the ordeal ended with Mitchell in custody, facing four charges, including felony fleeing or attempting to elude law enforcement, resisting an officer without violence, speeding on the beach, and riding outside the designated beach driving area. His bond was set at $4,000.

Recent findings suggest that and just like that, another dangerous electric bicycle criminal was brought to justice. This was clearly a success story like no other, and American streets are now safer.

Now, before anyone gets too worked up, let’s be clear: I’m not suggesting that e-bike riders should be allowed to ignore traffic laws, endanger pedestrians, or flee from police. Reports indicate that Mitchell was riding recklessly around beachgoers, including children, and that’s certainly something worth addressing. And once he allegedly decided to flee from deputies, he turned what could have been a minor infraction into a much more serious situation.

But can we also acknowledge how absurd this whole thing is?

We’ve reached a point where a 75-year-old man riding a bicycle at 16 mph can end up the subject of a police pursuit and felony charges, while we’ve largely accepted that multi-ton vehicles routinely kill and seriously injure people on our roads as an unavoidable cost of modern transportation.

Every day, drivers speed through neighborhoods, roll through stop signs, stare at their phones, and operate vehicles capable of killing pedestrians with a moment’s inattention. Or perhaps I shouldn’t say ‘capable’, but rather that they do. 40,000 people every year die in the US from car violence. Yet somehow, electric bicycles have become one of the great transportation menaces of our time, despite contributing much, much less to major bodily harm or death.

Industry observers note that and yes, there are absolutely legitimate concerns about dangerous riding. I’ve repeatedly argued that we need better enforcement, especially when it comes to teenagers riding high-powered electric dirt bikes and e-motos at 40 mph (64 km/h) down sidewalks and bike paths. Those aren’t electric bicycles, and treating them as such has created a real problem for everyone.

But if we’re going to devote police resources to cracking down on dangerous two-wheeled behavior, perhaps we could start there instead of turning a 1 mph beach ride into the crime of the century.

What is absurd is that he didn't simply stop and follow the officer's directions to slow down. If he is going to try to flee from the police by riding dangerously including going against traffic then he should face charges. As presumably a first time offender, he'll be given probation if he agrees not to do it again.

To be fair, Mitchell’s alleged behavior after being stopped certainly didn’t help his case. But the larger point remains: our priorities around road safety have become wildly distorted.

We’ve normalized the dangers of cars so thoroughly that we barely blink at the daily carnage they cause, yet we’re increasingly treating comparatively low-speed electric bicycles as an existential threat to public safety.

Recent findings suggest that I’m all for enforcing sensible e-bike rules. I’m all for throwing the book at major infractions and scofflaws who pose a public menace. But I’m also for applying a little perspective.

It has been revealed that because if a 75-year-old man riding an electric bicycle at 16 mph is among our most pressing transportation safety concerns, then I have some very good news about the state of our roads. But unfortunately, there is no good news to share today.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Latest research suggests that caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements are associated with significantly higher risks of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attack in young adults.
  • The findings, to be presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 November 6–9 in Chicago, are preliminary and can’t prove that energy drinks cause heart problems.
  • Still, the results highlight concerning cardiovascular effects of these popular products, particularly among adults under 35 who consume them regularly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Latest research suggests that caffeinated energy drinks and stimulant supplements are associated with significantly higher risks of serious heart problems, including cardiac arrest and heart attack in young adults.

The findings, to be presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026 November 6–9 in Chicago, are preliminary and can’t prove that energy drinks cause heart problems.

Still, the results highlight concerning cardiovascular effects of these popular products, particularly among adults under 35 who consume them regularly.

“These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk,” study author Sai Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine in Charlottesville, VA, stated in a news release.

Industry observers note that “For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can swiftly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it’s important for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products,” Samayamanthula continued.

Researchers from the University of Virginia School of Medicine analyzed 28,345 reports submitted to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) between 2017 and 2025.

Of these, 854 involved caffeinated energy drinks or stimulant supplements, while the remaining reports involved non-stimulant products.

It has been revealed that compared with non-stimulant products, cardiac arrest was reported approximately 11 times more often with energy drinks and stimulant supplements. Heart attacks were reported 4.5 times more often, while ventricular arrhythmias and palpitations were reported about four times more frequently.

Nearly 45% of heart-related reports involved adults ages 18 to 34.

“Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products. In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products,” Samayamanthula stated.

It has been revealed that gregory M. Marcus, MD, professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine, and chair of the 2026 AHA scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease, wasn’t involved in the study, but noted the research “raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system.”.

“Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis,” Marcus mentioned in a news release.

“More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events.”.

According to recent reports, cheng-Han Chen, MD, board certified interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center in Laguna Hills, CA, mentioned the findings, although concerning, are not surprising. Chen wasn’t involved in the study.

“We know that energy drinks can have significant effects on the cardiovascular system, primarily because of their stimulant properties,” he told Healthline.

Industry observers note that “Caffeine can increase blood pressure and heart rate, while other ingredients, such as guarana and taurine, may further contribute to cardiovascular stimulation and increased stress hormone levels. What is particularly concerning is the potential for these products to trigger serious complications, including abnormal heart rhythms, especially in people with underlying cardiovascular conditions.”.

Sources indicate that chen agreed that occasional energy drink consumption is unlikely to have long-term consequences for heart health in most healthy individuals. However, he said that “frequent or excessive consumption can potentially increase the risk of hypertension and cardiac arrhythmias.”.

In a recent development, an AHA scientific statement published in July 2026 notes that up to 400 milligrams of caffeine daily is generally considered safe for most healthy adults. That’s roughly equivalent to four or five 8-ounce cups of brewed coffee, depending on how it’s prepared.

However, some energy drinks contain up to three times as much caffeine per fluid ounce as brewed coffee.

Certain energy drinks may also contain stimulants, such as guarana, yerba mate, theobromine, synephrine, and yohimbine.

These ingredients may compound caffeine’s effects on the cardiovascular system.

According to recent reports, “Caffeine stimulates the cardiovascular system, primarily by increasing sympathetic nervous system activity. This can cause the heart to beat faster, raise blood pressure, and increase the workload on the heart,” Chen stated.

It has been revealed that “Energy drinks may contain additional stimulants, such as guarana and taurine, which can further increase blood pressure and stress hormone levels. With excessive consumption, these effects can become more pronounced and potentially interfere with the heart’s normal electrical activity, increasing the risk of abnormal heart rhythms. People with underlying cardiovascular conditions, particularly hypertension or a predisposition to arrhythmias, may be especially vulnerable to these effects.”.

Other research has echoed these concerns. A 2025 review suggests that high-volume energy drink consumption can prolong the heart’s QTc interval, increase blood pressure, and raise heart rate beyond the effects of caffeine alone.

“There is growing concern about the cardiovascular effects of energy drinks and stimulant-containing supplements, particularly among younger adults,” Chen remarked.

“One challenge is that younger individuals may not recognize that these products can have significant effects on their heart and blood pressure, especially when consumed frequently or in combination with other caffeinated products.”.

Young adults accounted for a substantial portion of the FDA reports included in the study, highlighting potential cardiovascular concerns for this age group.

People with existing heart conditions, a history of irregular heart rhythms, or heightened caffeine sensitivity may face additional risks. Those with undiagnosed genetic heart conditions may also be vulnerable.

A 2024 study identified cases of sudden cardiac arrest occurring shortly after energy drink consumption, particularly among people with underlying inherited heart conditions.

“As a cardiologist, I am particularly concerned about people who may have underlying cardiovascular conditions that have not yet been diagnosed,” Chen said.

It has been revealed that “Excessive stimulant intake can potentially trigger symptoms such as palpitations, chest discomfort, and lightheadedness. In susceptible individuals, it may also increase the risk of more serious complications, including abnormal heart rhythms.”.

Additionally, combining energy drinks with strenuous exercise or alcohol may introduce additional cardiovascular risks.

The findings suggest an association between energy drinks, stimulant supplements, and reported cardiovascular events, but they are preliminary and do not establish cause and effect.

The FDA database also relied on voluntary adverse-event reports, meaning some events may never be reported, while others may receive disproportionate attention.

Researchers also do not yet know how many people consumed these products without experiencing any problems. Without this variable, the reports cannot establish actual risk.

Industry observers note that other factors, including underlying health conditions, medications, and lifestyle habits, may also influence the results. More systematic research and controlled clinical trials are needed.

For most healthy adults, consuming up to 400 milligrams of caffeine per day is generally considered safe.

However, Chen noted that individual tolerance for caffeine may vary, and people with underlying cardiovascular conditions, particularly high blood pressure or abnormal heart rhythms, may need to limit or avoid caffeine altogether.

“Energy drinks can vary considerably in their caffeine content and serving sizes,” Chen said.

Sources indicate that “Depending on the product, a single can may contain anywhere from 80 to 300 milligrams of caffeine. This means that consuming even one or two energy drinks can put someone close to or above the recommended daily limit, particularly when combined with coffee, tea, or other caffeinated supplements.”.

Seek emergency medical attention if you experience chest pain, particularly if it’s accompanied by shortness of breath, fainting, or other symptoms of a possible heart attack.

If you live with a heart condition, ask your doctor about your daily caffeine intake to determine whether you need to cut back.

According to Chen, warning signs of excessive stimulant intake may include:.

“Depending on the severity of these symptoms, medical attention may be necessary,” he noted.

Still, most people may not need to give up caffeine entirely. Monitoring your habits could help protect your heart health. This may include:.

Recent findings suggest that “I encourage people to read product labels carefully and be aware of their total daily caffeine consumption,” Chen said. “I particularly recommend that people with underlying cardiovascular conditions avoid energy drinks.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Genesis just added a new member to its growing family. the 2028 Genesis G80 Hybrid. It’s Genesis’s second-ever hybrid, to be precise—and the G80 Hybrid, along with the related GV80 Hybrid, will showcase the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrid system with a liquid-cooled battery.

Hyundai debuted its new liquid-cooled hybrid battery at a preview event on Tuesday, November 17, in Los Angeles, offering the media the chance to understand what makes it notable. By outperforming air-cooled systems with regard to temperature management, it unlocks higher peak discharge output and taps into more of the battery’s available power. Genesis first revealed its next-generation 2.5 Turbo Hybrid System for the GV80 Hybrid a few months ago, and now, we’re getting more details about how the same system will perform under the hood of the G80 Hybrid.

The electric-assisted 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four produces a hearty 347 horsepower—16 percent more than the standard four-cylinder G80 model—and 391 pound-feet of torque. The engine will be mated to a seven-speed automatic transmission, with a choice of “manual” or “smart” adjustable regenerative braking settings; the smart setting will automatically adjust regenerative braking levels based on navigation information and traffic conditions. The G80 Hybrid will come in rear-wheel drive.

It has been revealed that genesis claims the G80 Hybrid will feature 30-percent improved fuel economy over a comparable G80 model with 19-inch wheels, with driving range estimates extending to over 500 miles. Since these claims are based on internal testing, we’ll have to wait to see what final EPA fuel economy and driving range estimates are.

Want to be able to spot a G80 Hybrid in the wild? There are a few small changes to the exterior that should help you spot one. There’s a redesigned 3-D grille, fresh 18- and 20-inch wheel designs, and a range of new exterior colors; you can choose from Wadden Gray, Milos Blue, and Barolo Red. If you want to stand out from other G80 Hybrid models, a Prestige Black variant will be available with a blacked-out exterior and interior, plus exclusive Black Ash Wood and alloy wheels.

Sources indicate that inside, the G80 Hybrid is identical to the standard G80, with Nappa leather seating surfaces and distinct quilting patterns on different trim levels. You’ll also find the Genesis-familiar 27-inch OLED integrated instrument cluster and navigation display, as well as the comprehensive suite of advanced driver assistance technologies the brand bakes into its upcoming models.

Genesis has yet to announce pricing details or a production date for the 2028 G80 Hybrid, but it seems likely they’ll start to reach dealers sometime in late 2027. Interested in seeing the Genesis G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid yourself before then? It will be displayed at the 2026 LA Auto Show during its public days, which run from November 20–29.

The Holidays on a Tight Budget

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • “Although we had no money, I was rich as I could be, in my coat of many colors, my mama made for me.” —Dolly Parton.
  • According to recent reports, in the song “Times A-Getting Hard, Boys,” Pete Seeger famously captured the tune from Carl Sandburg’s collection, revised by Lee Hays, referring to the debt-ridden farmers who abandoned their land and migrated to California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

“Although we had no money, I was rich as I could be, in my coat of many colors, my mama made for me.” —Dolly Parton.

According to recent reports, in the song “Times A-Getting Hard, Boys,” Pete Seeger famously captured the tune from Carl Sandburg’s collection, revised by Lee Hays, referring to the debt-ridden farmers who abandoned their land and migrated to California. It was the Dust Bowl, yet another Depression-era tragedy.

Granted, we are not close to the Great Depression now. But the wealth gap is near historic highs, and for much of the nation, economic hardship is on the front burner, just in time for the holidays.

Bottom line: Families are paying more for just about everything that matters most. So how can we travel, host, and preserve our holiday traditions under this kind of financial stress?

According to recent reports, we are all influenced by the idyllic Hallmark portrayal of the holidays on TV and social media. It’s easy to fall prey to ideals of perfection, only to have our expectations dashed by reality.

Let’s face it. Even in great economic times, the holidays are stressful, laced with conflict and inevitable disappointment.

We begin with the adults. As the flight attendant states, “If the cabin pressure drops, put your own oxygen mask on first, then help the person next to you.” We are better at managing our kids’ stress when we first take care of our own.

Kids don’t worry about money the way adults do, but they feel our stress, and it has an impact on them.

For all of us, adults and kids alike, self-care is essential: eating well, exercising, getting restorative sleep, and making time for meditation or relaxation. In short, finding (free) ways to reduce stress.

Stress due to financial strain is not all that different than stress induced by other psychosocial factors.

But one thing is different. Even in therapy, talking about one’s finances can be rare. Clinicians will hear about all sorts of complex complications, but some research has shown that rarely, if ever, does a patient talk about money—their income, net worth, debt, and attendant issues for the family.

So, how can we have meaningful conversations with our kids and other family members about what we can afford this year?

Recent findings suggest that tailor the conversation to your child’s age. Remember that younger kids don’t need details about the family budget, but they do need reassurance. School-age kids can understand trade-offs, and they often like being part of the solution. While teens can handle more nuanced conversations about financial matters, they’re also most likely to feel the sting of comparison with peers.

Before we change anything this year, we need to know what our kids, young and old, are thinking.

Gatherings are super important: Coming together does more than we think. A review of 148 studies following more than 308,000 people found that those with stronger social relationships had a 50 percent higher likelihood of surviving over the study’s period than those with weaker ties, and this finding remained consistent across age, sex, and even initial health. Gatherings save lives.

Try these suggestions for keeping the social ties strong despite financial challenges.

Remember that giving is as vital for the giver as the receiver. In a study during the COVID-19 pandemic, 777 people were asked to perform three acts of kindness each week for two weeks. Those assigned to be kind to others experienced significant decreases in depression, anxiety, and loneliness. Here are some ideas to kick around for giving.

It has been revealed that these are not easy times. But when we share our hardships, we fare better. Don’t worry alone!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you wake up tomorrow as the esteemed Lord Mayor of London, you’ll want to make a properly dignified entrance. To make sure your arrival turns the right heads, Electrogenic has taken the Mayor’s 1973 Roll-Royce Phantom VI and turned it into a properly traditional standard-bearer with modern electric power.

The stately, stylish, and silent electric Rolls-Royce car made its public debut at last month’s Salon Privé weekend at Blenheim Palace, where it joined a growing fleet of classic Rollers that have received Elctrogenic’s electric conversion, including the stunning Mulliner-bodied 1929 Phantom II that we covered back in 2023.

In a recent development, for this project, Electrogenic carefully removed the internal combustion-based engine, transmission, and fuel system from the City of London Corporation’s official ’73 Phantom VI limo and replaced it with a 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motor putting out 310 Nm (~230 lb-ft) of torque. Sharp-eyed readers will note those numbers are significantly lower than what you’d expect from the 6.2L L410 V8 fitted with twin SU carburetors (as it was in the standard ’73 IV), but since those numbers were never officially published, we would say that the power available from the upcoming electric drivetrain is similarly adequate for Mayoral use.

Power for the electric motor comes from a 62 kWh li-ion battery fitted under the hood bonnet, and offers more than enough range to get the Lord Mayor to their appointments in and around the city.

To ensure the heads of the heads of the city don’t bob in an undignified manner while on parade, Electrogenic added a “ceremonial” drive mode that trims power and torque and softens the throttle map, so the chauffeur can more easily hold the crawling pace demanded by civic processions and state occasions.

“We were honored to be asked to electrify this significant motor car, and to play a part in the City of London Corporation’s journey to net zero,” claims Steve Drummond, chief executive of Electrogenic. “When it was rolled out in the late 1960s, the Rolls-Royce VI was the most refined and dignified limousine on the road. Now, thanks to electrification, its core character has been enhanced further: it is whisper quiet, effortless to drive with swift performance, and emits zero tailpipe emissions.”.

It's notable for government to be seen to follow it's own policy.

A standard complaint by oil lobbyists is that government vehicles aren't electrified.

The Phantom was converted as part of the Corporation’s broader effort to achieve a net zero carbon emissions goal from its own operations in 2027.

#87176. The Lame Duck: A Leader's Exit Can Be Bad or Good

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

The Lame Duck: A Leader's Exit Can Be Bad or Good

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Industry observers note that it happens all the time.
  • What happens when a leader mentally disengages from their position and takes a “who cares” attitude?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 21, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Industry observers note that it happens all the time. A leader’s time in the role is coming to an end. A leader who is completing the end of tenure in a top-level leadership position can either do an organization great harm or much good. What happens when a leader is a lame duck, with a known date for terminating their tenure? It all depends on the leader’s intent, their motivation, and how the leader’s team deals with it.

Neglect. What happens when a leader mentally disengages from their position and takes a “who cares” attitude? In one instance, a department director who was finishing his last few months simply stopped leading—communicating much less, canceling meetings that focused on moving the company forward, and not providing much information or feedback to direct reports. The organization came to a virtual standstill that lasted for a while, and it took latest, energetic leadership to recover.

According to recent reports, trashing the Place. Even worse, a leader can decide to cause real damage. This can occur when the leader has been fired or feels unfairly treated. The leader might end promising and/or profitable projects. Resources might be rerouted to the leader’s benefit. More subtly, the leader might pit team members against one another and create a toxic work culture.

Motivational Malaise. A leader’s lack of interest and activity as they come to the end of their tenure can be contagious, affecting the motivation of other employees (“If the leader doesn’t seem to care, why should I?” “The leader is taking a lot of personal time off, so I guess it’s OK.”). The leader’s negativity or simple disinterest can be infectious and affect the motivation of others.

Recent findings suggest that allow Others to Step Up to Leadership. A good leader develops leadership capacity in others. When a leader is exiting, it is crucial to provide opportunities for direct reports to take on leadership roles and activities. A much-celebrated CEO who was retiring told me that he knew that the organization would be in good hands after his departure because he had worked to develop his successors’ leadership. Delegating responsibility and sharing the leadership is the key to developing followers into leaders.

Strengthen Existing Processes. When a leader’s departure is inevitable, it is a good time for the leader to do a comprehensive evaluation of the organization’s operations. Rather than winding things down, it’s a good time to focus on improvement. What could be working better? What upcoming initiatives should be fast-tracked? Rather than taking it easy, the departing leader should ramp things up.

Recent findings suggest that leave a Legacy. An effective leader who is in the waning stages of tenure needs to realize that it is important to continue efforts to improve the organization and its operations. This is the legacy that a good leader leaves behind. The departure should be positive, formative, and free from regrets.

A first-of-its-kind international food pyramid, developed by 22 leading nutritionists from Europe, Canada, the United States, and Australia, was published in Advances in Nutrition in September.

This latest food pyramid emphasizes plant-based protein sources, cooking with plant-based oils, and healthier sugars and carbohydrates.

It also echoes the traditional food pyramid used in the United States since 1992.

Industry observers note that the new pyramid breaks away from the Trump administration’s updated nutritional guidelines, which are part of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s Make America Health Again (MAHA) agenda and prioritize red meat over plants.

The new pyramid was designed by a research team led by Brigham Young University professor Karen Della Corte. The researchers noted that this is the first international food pyramid that is designed to reflect scientific agreement across multiple countries and cultures.

Della Corte and researchers from the International Carbohydrate Quality Consortium (ICQC), compared dietary guidelines from multiple countries, including:.

They also analyzed evidence from more than 250 scientific publications, while drawing on the EAT-Lancet Planetary Health Diet to identify principles of healthy eating that may be shared.

The new pyramid highlights three guidelines:.

While the pyramid emphasizes plant-based proteins, it doesn’t exclude animal proteins.

“I find the new international food pyramid a more practical and aligned approach for the prevention of chronic disease,” noted Michelle Routhenstein, Preventive Cardiology Dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the creation of the food pyramid.

“The upcoming international food pyramid places greater emphasis on food quality and the importance of building meals around nutrient-dense plant foods, while still allowing room for lean animal proteins such as fish, poultry, eggs, and yogurt,” she added.

Sources indicate that while the latest pyramid and the current U.S. dietary guidelines differ in many ways, they also agree on certain factors.

For example, both sets of guidelines discourage added sugars, refined carbs, and highly processed snacks.

Industry observers note that the differences between the two mainly lie in their emphasis on specific sources of protein and fat. For example, the fresh pyramid prioritizes plant-based proteins, while the U.S. guidelines place greater emphasis on animal proteins, including red meat.

According to recent reports, while both sets of recommendations advise limiting saturated fat, the new pyramid emphasizes unsaturated plant oils, whereas the U.S. guidelines also include butter and beef tallow as cooking fat options.

Sources indicate that routhenstein noted that an important distinction is that this new pyramid goes beyond simply telling people to eat more protein or fewer carbohydrates. Instead, it encourages people to consider the quality and sources of those nutrients.

However, the main emphasis of both guidelines is encouraging people to eat fewer ultra-processed foods and more natural or “real” foods.

Routhenstein told Healthline that research consistently demonstrates that plant-forward eating patterns, including the Mediterranean and DASH diets, are associated with better cardiovascular health and a lower risk of heart disease.

Plant foods provide fiber, potassium, antioxidants, and other beneficial compounds that can help support healthy cholesterol levels, blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood vessel function.

“This is not to say that protein and fat are unimportant, but their sources matter,” Routhenstein stated.

In a statement from BYU, Della Corte shared the following tips for incorporating the upcoming pyramid’s recommendations into your diet:.

The pyramid is a framework, not a personalized prescription. If you have questions about your individual nutritional needs, you can speak with your healthcare professional or a licensed dietitian.

“It is vital to recognize that plant-forward does not mean vegan or vegetarian. The amount and sources of animal protein should be considered to ensure they align with an individual’s cardiometabolic goals and lab targets,” Routhenstein stated.
